long_biography.plain_text:
When Daniel Shamoon's father proposed a summer in the accounts department, the young hotelier offered to open a beach restaurant at Puente Romano instead. A successful launch would let him spend the holiday running it. He combined dining, drinks and music in one venue, drawing on his father's experience of London nightclubs.

Staff development became another part of his work. After taking over Hermitage Bay in Antigua, Shamoon kept the original team and sent employees to train at other hotels in the family portfolio. They returned with new skills to use at the resort.
